drafted_from: tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (the workflow:set-up-a-checked-repository row: input_schema and steps read-the-repository and pin-the-data with their submit shapes); no test names it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:set-up-a-checked-repository on the folder bakery-site with my registry file checks/registry.json and my check command ./run-checks.sh."
no_lists_because: The workflow writes files inside the repository (capabilities.json, a pin file, retired-paths.json) and entries in the person's own registry files; it names no Trillion list.
instructions: 1. Have your repository folder, your check registry file or files, and the command that runs your commit checks on staged files; optionally your hook installer command, the product folder of DATA files a program reads, and its pin file.
2. Say "Run workflow:set-up-a-checked-repository" with repository, registries and check_command.

3. It reads the repository's READMEs, writes capabilities.json (one row per folder, only from what each folder's README says; it asks you about any folder with no README line), pins the DATA files with tool:pin-files-by-content, writes retired-paths.json, and adds the repository to each registry in that file's own schema.
4. It stages those files and runs your check command; a refusal is fixed in the repository's own files, never by changing a check, and it reports passed true only when every check passed.
